summary: One plain file pattern, with no {a,b} choices in it.
One file or directory in the file tree.
A question a stopped job needs a person to answer, with a message, the form of the answer, and a preview of the change.
One piece of work a caller asks of VFS, saved only when it stops to ask a person and carried on with the answer.
The object that holds the file tree, checks every call and sends it to the storage that holds the path.
Storage attached at a path in the file tree.
A rule the application writes as a function, which sees each step before it runs and allows it, denies it, or asks a person.
The record VFS keeps of one conversation with an agent, which remembers the files the agent has seen and where its shell is.
A note a session keeps that the agent has seen one path, and what was there when it did.
One action VFS is about to take, described before it happens so a policy can decide whether it may run.
An object that keeps entries and answers the calls on them, attached to the file tree as a mount.
One message from the user and everything the agent does to answer it, as one part of a session.
A short code, named for version and id, that stands for one file at one version, so a change can require it.
